what: Applied Industrial Technologies distributes the parts that keep factories running: bearings, power transmission components, seals, hoses and fluid power systems, delivered from hundreds of branches.
customers: Manufacturers, mines, food plants and other industrial operators needing replacement parts quickly.
money: bearings and power transmission parts from local branches
fluid power, automation and flow control systems
moat: A branch network close to plants, where a broken bearing means a stopped production line and the distributor who has it in stock wins regardless of price.
risks: Industrial production drives demand, and it has been soft
A 8.3% net margin, normal for distribution but thin
25 times earnings for a business growing in the mid single digits
opportunities: Revenue grew from $3.8B to $5.0B in four years with $422M of free cash flow
Analysts see about 32% upside, with 6 covering the stock
Automation and fluid power projects earn higher margins than commodity parts and are a growing share
watch: Organic sales growth and the Engineered Solutions share of the mix.
